title: SBI PO Mains — Mock Test 3
description: Full-length 100-question mock simulating the latest SSC CGL Tier-1 pattern. 60 minutes total, no sectional timing, 2 marks/Q, -0.5 negative. Includes 5 inline Current-Affairs questions in the GA section (FDI 2025, CAD H1 2025-26, Bihar CM resignation, GRP Conference, India-UAE bilateral trade) — refreshable from the admin CA pool.

questions.stem: In a code, 'GREEN' is written as 'IGTHHP'. Wait — different lengths. Use 'GREEN' = 'IDTHHP' (each letter shifts +2 then reverses each pair)? Too complex. Let me use simple shift +2: GREEN+2 = ITGGP. How is 'BLACK' coded?
questions.explanation: Each letter shifts +2: B→D, L→N, A→C, C→E, K→M ⟹ DNCEM.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: If A=1, B=2 ... Z=26, what is the SUM of letter values in 'STAR'?
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: In a code, '361' means 'PEN BOOK PAPER', '462' means 'PEN BLACK INK', '532' means 'INK GOOD PEN'. What is the code for 'PEN'?
questions.explanation: 361 ∩ 462 ∩ 532 = digits common to all three = {2}. The common WORD across all three is PEN. So PEN = 2.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: If 'NORTH' is coded as 'OPSUI' (each letter shifts +1), how is 'SOUTH' coded?
questions.explanation: Each letter shifts +1: S→T, O→P, U→V, T→U, H→I ⟹ TPVUI.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: In a code, 'CAR' is written as 'XZI' (mirror cipher). How is 'BUS' coded?
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: Find the next term: AB, EF, IJ, MN, ?
questions.explanation: Each pair starts 4 letters after the previous: A→E (+4), E→I (+4), I→M (+4), M→Q (+4). So next pair starts at Q ⟹ QR.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: Pointing to a man, Riya says, 'He is the brother of my mother's only daughter.' How is the man related to Riya?
questions.explanation: Riya's mother's only daughter = Riya herself. The brother of Riya = Riya's brother.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: If P is the son of Q, R is the wife of P, and S is the daughter of R, how is S related to Q?
questions.explanation: P is Q's son. R is P's wife. S is R's daughter — also P's daughter (since R = P's wife). So S is the daughter of Q's son = Q's granddaughter.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: A walks 5 km north, turns east and walks 12 km, then turns south and walks 5 km. How far is A from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Net displacement: north 5 − 5 = 0; east = 12. Distance = 12 km.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: A man walks 3 km west, then 4 km south, and finally 6 km east. What is his shortest distance from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Net west = 3 − 6 = −3 (i.e. 3 km east). Net south = 4. Distance = √(9 + 16) = √25 = 5 km.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem:
Statements: All artists are creative. Some creative people are entrepreneurs.
Conclusions:
I. Some artists are entrepreneurs.
II. All entrepreneurs are creative.
questions.explanation:
I. Only SOME creative are entrepreneurs — that subset might not include any artists. NOT guaranteed.
II. Converse fallacy. NOT guaranteed.
Neither follows.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem:
Statements: All triangles are polygons. All polygons are shapes.
Conclusions:
I. All triangles are shapes.
II. Some shapes are triangles.
questions.explanation:
I. Triangles ⊂ polygons ⊂ shapes ⟹ all triangles are shapes. FOLLOWS.
II. Triangles exist as shapes ⟹ some shapes are triangles. FOLLOWS.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem:
Statements: Some teachers are scientists. No scientist is illiterate.
Conclusions:
I. Some teachers are not illiterate.
II. No teacher is illiterate.
questions.explanation:
I. Some teachers are scientists, no scientist is illiterate ⟹ those teachers are not illiterate. FOLLOWS.
II. Other teachers (not scientists) might be illiterate. NOT guaranteed.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem:
Statements: All papers are books. No book is digital.
Conclusions:
I. No paper is digital.
II. Some books are not digital.
questions.explanation:
I. Papers ⊂ books, books disjoint from digital ⟹ papers disjoint from digital ⟹ no paper is digital. FOLLOWS.
II. Books exist, none are digital ⟹ at least some books are not digital. FOLLOWS.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem:
Statements: Some birds fly. All flying things have wings.
Conclusions:
I. Some birds have wings.
II. All birds have wings.
questions.explanation:
I. Some birds fly, all flying things have wings ⟹ those birds have wings. FOLLOWS.
II. Birds that don't fly might not have wings. NOT guaranteed.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem:
Statements: A > B; C ≤ B; D < C; E = A
Conclusions:
I. E > D
II. A > C
questions.explanation:
I. E = A > B ≥ C > D ⟹ E > D. FOLLOWS.
II. A > B ≥ C ⟹ A > C. FOLLOWS.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: Five friends — A, B, C, D, E — sit in a row facing North. A sits at the right end. C sits to the left of B but not adjacent. E sits between A and B. Where does D sit?
questions.explanation: A@5. E between A and B requires B and A flanking E ⟹ B@3, E@4. C left of B but not adjacent: C@1. D at remaining position 2. Final: C@1, D@2, B@3, E@4, A@5. D is at position 2 = second from left.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: Six people — P, Q, R, S, T, U — sit around a circular table facing the centre. P sits opposite T. Q is immediate right of P. R is immediate left of P. S is between R and T (when traversing anti-clockwise from R). Who sits opposite Q?
questions.explanation: P@1, T@4 (opposite). Q@2 (clockwise from P). R@6 (anti-clockwise). Going anti-clockwise from R(6) toward T(4): seat 5. So S@5. U@3 (remaining). Opposite Q(2) = (2+3) mod 6 = 5 → S.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: Five people — V, W, X, Y, Z — live on 5 floors (1=ground, 5=top). X lives on floor 5. V lives on floor 2. Y lives immediately above W. Where does Z live?
questions.explanation: X=5, V=2. Y=W+1, Y and W from {1,3,4}. Possible (W,Y) pairs in {1,3,4}: (3,4). So W=3, Y=4. Z = remaining = 1.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: Four friends — P, Q, R, S — were born in different months: January, March, May, July. P was born after Q. R was born immediately before P. Who was born in January?
questions.explanation: R immediately before P ⟹ R, P consecutive in month order with R earlier. Q before P. So order: Q, R, P (or with S anywhere). Smallest assignment: Q=Jan, R=Mar, P=May, S=July. Q in January.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem:
What is the cost of a notebook?
I. 5 notebooks and 3 pens cost ₹130.
II. 1 notebook costs twice as much as 1 pen.
questions.explanation: I alone: 5N + 3P = 130 — two unknowns. II alone: N = 2P — one equation, two unknowns. Together: 5(2P) + 3P = 130 ⟹ 13P = 130 ⟹ P = 10, N = 20. Sufficient.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem:
Who is the tallest among P, Q, R, S?
I. P is taller than Q but shorter than R.
II. S is taller than R.
questions.explanation: I: Q < P < R. Doesn't tell us about S. II: S > R. Together: Q < P < R < S ⟹ S is tallest. Sufficient together.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: How many squares can be drawn using 6 horizontal and 6 vertical equally-spaced lines (forming a 5x5 grid)?
questions.explanation: Squares of size 1×1: 25, of size 2×2: 16, of size 3×3: 9, of size 4×4: 4, of size 5×5: 1. Total = 25+16+9+4+1 = 55.
questions.subject: REASONING

questions.stem: Which of the following best captures the author's stance on PSBs?
questions.passage_context: The role of public-sector banks (PSBs) in India remains a topic of vigorous debate. Defenders argue that PSBs are essential vehicles for financial inclusion, particularly in rural and semi-urban areas where private banks have historically been slow to expand. Critics point to a long history of bad loans, governance shortcomings, and an over-reliance on government recapitalisation. Recent reforms have tried to address both concerns: governance frameworks have been tightened, capital adequacy has improved, and PSBs have been encouraged to merge so that they operate at competitive scale. Yet the structural question — whether full or partial privatisation would serve depositors better — remains unresolved. The answer likely lies in a careful balance: preserving the social mandate where it matters most while exposing PSBs to the discipline of market competition where it does not.
options: PSBs should be preserved exactly as they are.
Balance social mandate with market discipline.
PSBs should be replaced by foreign banks.
questions.explanation: The closing line: 'preserving the social mandate where it matters most while exposing PSBs to the discipline of market competition where it does not.'
questions.subject: ENGLISH

(A) The benefits of this approach quickly became apparent.

questions.explanation: Order: C (intro: company introduced 4-day week) → D (initial scepticism) → A (benefits became apparent) → E (3 months in, data spoke) → B (specific results). 3rd = A.

questions.stem: Convert to indirect speech: He asked, 'Are you coming with me?'
options: He asked if I was coming with him.
He asked if I am coming with him.
He asked that was I coming with him.
He asked whether you are coming with him.
questions.explanation: Yes/no question + past reporting: use 'if' / 'whether'. Pronoun shifts: 'you' → 'I'; 'me' → 'him'. Tense shifts: 'are' → 'was'.
